title: Contract transition in place
goal: Introduce the final supported consumer/implementer surface and make the existing scope, audit and generator code use it from its current location, as the single documented pre-1.0 contract transition.
context: Architecture phase B (revision 2, D7–D10, D12). Approximate size: L. Detailed PHP signatures and tasks are authored in a separate phase-design session from the fixed semantics in knowledge/architecture. Files of the future modules stay where they are; only contracts, core namespaces and call paths change. Detailed on 2026-10-11 into P2.1–P2.15 under owner answers M14/M15 (D15–D17): 0.7.0 is no compatibility constraint; the reference is implemented exactly.

consumes: P1 evidence, parity harness and boundary scans
produces: #[Api]/#[Spi] attributes on the whole supported surface and an attribute-driven, member-aware manifest generator
Typed AzGuard\AzGuard entry and generated facade methods
Declaration-only Plugin SPI and named contracts for every slot with checked closures

Scope algebra in core (mode enums, declaration slot, envelope, structural verification, typed resource mapping) with the existing scope code implementing AssignmentScopeEvaluator and the exact-query capability
ChangeParticipant with append-only owned-table writer, storage descriptor and identity-column helper, with the existing audit journal re-targeted to it
Typed module options; StoresGrants, GateMode, boot(), BasePlugin and DependsOnPlugins retired; writer capabilities in PanelSchema; Filament on neutral contracts
Context and Tenancy namespaces; opaque state tokens with the payload rule; azg_ field reservation
A short migration instruction for AI agents covering every P2 change of a supported symbol, member, DSL, config key, command behavior or identity value (docs/upgrade.md, D16)
boundaries: Core owns mandatory stages, the scope algebra and the only authority writer
Core never calls implementer SPI with named arguments
No public coordinator, session, StorageMutation or module type in core signatures
No macros, module bus, plugin-ID dependency or new generic workflow mechanism
Parity, consistency and transactional suites stay green after every step

include: AzGuard entry, facade, Attributes, manifest generator and ApiManifestTest
Contracts, Context, Tenancy, Panels compiler/builder, Authorization stages and visibility compiler
Changes pipeline/validator/event construction, Storage descriptor and schema helper
Existing scope, audit and generator code adapted to the new contracts in place
Filament call sites using DatabaseSource, CurrentContext and GateBridge internals
exclude: Moving files into modules/ roots or splitting installers (P3)
New authorization features or relaxed exact-query semantics
One interface or Composer package per internal service
Reopening names or shapes after the candidate

pitfalls: Consumer compatibility differs from implementer/subclass compatibility
The exact-query split of VisibilityScope must keep the P1 parity matrix unchanged
Readonly runtime inputs may still borrow mutable host models
An owned-table writer returning a connection or builder defeats its boundary
A facade without generated methods evades the manifest
Opaque StateToken serialization must keep the payload state keys of knowledge/contracts#tokens
P1 report-mode allowlists fail on stale entries: remove an entry in the same commit as its fix
Module-owned types created in P2 live at interim src/ paths (D17); do not add module autoload roots

validation.procedure: Classify every supported type/member/override/facade method by attribute and verify signature closure; compile built-in and independent consumer contributions through the same slots; reject duplicate ids/keys, conflicting declarations, closure signature mismatches, unmet slot requirements, unchecked context writes and invariant-bypassing continuation/results; run the P1 parity, consistency, transactional and format suites with scope and audit behavior reached only through the new contracts.
validation.expect: I4, I6, I7, I8, I10, I11, I14 and I20 green; parity matrix verdicts unchanged except the 82 directory verdicts of I9 findings F1/F2, which now equal write admission; every P1 fixture change is deliberate and listed in its item result; allowlists hold only owner-P3 entries.

deliverables: Attributed API/SPI inventory incl. members, overrides, named-argument stance and enum classes
Final contract signatures for every slot and capability
AI-agent migration instruction and non-PHP contract changes (docs/upgrade.md)

sections.title: Mandatory design inputs
sections.text:
The detailing session for P2 reads these before authoring any item (`show` of this phase is the entry point; the list is mandatory):

```bash
P='python3 <task>/scripts/plan.py'; ID=2026.10.10-№1-AZGUARD-CORE-STABILIZATION
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section product
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section ownership
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section scope-boundary
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section extension-system
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section spi-catalog
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section operation-chains
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section persistence
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section api-compatibility
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section invariants
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section cost
$P get $ID knowledge/architecture --section risks
$P get $ID knowledge/contracts            # all sections (normative signatures)
$P get $ID knowledge/type-map            # all zones; rows with phase P2 are this phase's scope
$P get $ID knowledge/upgrade-map            # all sections (complete it)
$P get $ID knowledge/identities            # all sections
$P get $ID knowledge/target-structure            # rules
$P get $ID D4
$P get $ID D5
$P get $ID D7
$P get $ID D8
$P get $ID D9
$P get $ID D10
$P get $ID D13
```

Rules for the detailed items:

- Each item lists in `reads` (with `section`, `required: true`) the reference sections it implements; a phase-bound document that no item reads is reported by `design-done` (`phase_documents_unread`) and must be resolved before the phase counts as detailed.
- Items cite their type-map rows by current FQCN in `scope.include`; an item may not move, rename or re-mark a type differently from `knowledge/type-map`.
- If `design-done` reports a pack over the 256 KB budget, move the binding of a reference document from the phase to the items that read it (`plan.py unlink … --kind applies_to`, `plan.py link …`) — never drop the read.
- Every new or changed type is implemented exactly as in `knowledge/contracts`; any other signature is an amendment.

sections.title: Exit criterion
sections.text: All supported signatures and extension semantics have one stable owner; scope behavior, audit journaling and generators run only through the final contracts, so P3 can relocate them without inventing another public mechanism.
